name: WSFx Global Pay Ltd
title: WSFx Global Pay Ltd - 511147 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: FY26 revenue up 26% to ~INR111 crore and PAT up 77% to INR6.14 crore, but management flags Q1 FY27 leisure contraction of ~25% and a 0.6-0.8% net margin under pressure from new AD-II competition.

triggers.label: Leisure market down ~25% since March
triggers.quote: I can say 25% contraction has been there '25 March, April, May and we expect next one or two months to be a little challenging.

triggers.label: Trade remittance margins 20-30 bps
triggers.quote: In a trade remittance, it will maybe go down considerably maybe we'll looking at a 20-30 bps is the margins which we are looking at

triggers.quote: FEMA 401/2026 RBI circular materially expands the addressable market for AD II players.

triggers.label: RBI stopped fresh FFMC licences
triggers.quote: RBI has also stopped issuance of fresh FFMC licenses strengthening incumbents' position.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 26% to about INR111 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR6.14 crore, while Q4 growth slowed on macro and war-related travel weakness.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with revenue crossing about INR111 crore for the first time, PBT of INR8.03 crore and PAT of INR6.14 crore, and the company stated it remains debt-free. Q4 was hit by macro volatility, especially in March, from the US-Israel-Iran conflict and lower US student travel, though management said Q4 revenue still grew 22% and GTO grew 16%. Management highlighted the FEMA 401/2026 RBI circular, which expands AD-II scope to trade remittances and family maintenance and allows Forex Correspondent (FXC) appointments, and said it has recommended a 15% dividend. Management also acknowledged that rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup have taken share from forex cards in leisure travel, and that leisure market volumes contracted about 25% from March.

segments.name: Student
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver per management; overall market contracted about 20% in the year while the company gained share. Loan-funded students growing while own-funds students contracted after TCS was cut to 2%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Over 900 corporates served; management cited a 95.62% CAGR. Named clients include Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra and, recently, Adani.

segments.name: Retail / leisure
segments.commentary: Card business declined in FY26 on lower US student traffic and competition from rupee credit cards; leisure market down about 25% since March. Management described this as a calibrated, value-led push with a minimum margin per transaction.

segments.name: Prepaid cards
segments.commentary: Four products (three plastics and one digital-only, Uni-Z launched last month). Switch Card supports 30 currencies; Xplorer Metal card is by invitation. Samsung Pay and Google Pay tokenisation planned this year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 to be a challenging, linear quarter with leisure travel down roughly 25% from March, and expects the next one to two months to remain tough.
Trade remittances expected to become a material business in 12 to 18 months; family maintenance (about $3 billion market) to be a growth area.
FXC network expected to expand through the model over the next 12 to 15 months, with Spice Money group network and NBFC/retail partners as possible distribution.
Trade remittance margins expected 20-30 bps, below current blended levels, as competition rises.
Target to raise digital/automated share of transactions from about 60% to 80% this year.
Management did not give numerical FY27 targets for cards or revenue; it said Q2 to Q4 are peak months and FY27 mix will change materially.
capex_capacity: Network kept lean at 21+ branches (down from 35 when the CEO took over, 16 in COVID); expansion planned mainly through FXC appointments rather than owned branches.
Company is evaluating whether to apply for a PA-CB licence.
Working on multiple payment rails for faster, holiday-enabled remittances and a student fee-remittance platform.
Smart Agent Platform, FPaaS, Smart Corporate Platform and consumer app run on a unified payments stack.
demand_pricing: Q4 traffic hit in March by the US-Israel-Iran conflict; leisure market contracted about 25% from March to May 2026 per management.
Rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup and lounge perks have taken a large share of international spend (management estimate about 60%), with credit card spend outside LRS and TCS.
Management says it will not price at a loss; pricing uses interbank rates with a small card fulfilment fee on the Switch card.
B2B and corporate make up about 80-85% of business; partner commissions and referral fees are a larger share of costs.
Retail customer lifetime value is quoted at about INR1,000 of annual income per traveller versus high digital CAC.
Management expects more competition after the RBI circular, with margin pressure; trade remittances may run at 20-30 bps margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new RBI circular affect volumes, revenue and margins over the next one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scope has expanded to trade and non-trade current account transactions, with no negative impact from the circular itself, but competition will pressure margins. Trade remittance margins are expected at 20-30 bps; current net margin is 0.6-0.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will be most affected by the new regulations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split out the impact by segment. It said the new trade and family maintenance categories open new growth areas, and that retail/leisure faces the most pressure from credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with low-priced small players on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay competitive but will not work at a loss per transaction, citing a minimum margin policy and a digital platform for each segment. It acknowledged its retail pricing may not be the lowest.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise FY26 revenue, volume, customer and new-product breakdown; agent commissions versus branch revenue; CAC; card KPIs and FY27 targets
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only broad-based answers: B2B and corporate are 80-85% of business, partner commissions are higher as a B2B company, and digital CAC is high. It declined to give specific numbers and said detailed data would be shared through the company's written channel.

qa_highlights.question: How does Scapia (bank-sponsored card) compare, and how are rupee credit cards affecting forex cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cards hold a regulatory arbitrage (no LRS or TCS), that around 60% of international spend has moved to credit cards, and that the association has represented to RBI for parity. Forex cards are positioned on rate certainty for multi-currency travel; corporate and student segments do not use credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TCS cut to 2% for education remittances doing to the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2% TCS mainly hit own-fund students, while loan-funded students are growing; it called the change a relief and said zero TCS would be better for the priority-sector segment.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and payables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Pooja Mishra said the rise in current assets and liabilities reflects card-program customer wallet balances on both sides of the balance sheet. Capital turnover improved to 4.4x from 3.8x, and short-term borrowings are fixed-deposit-backed working capital lines, not structural debt.

risks_watch: Leisure and card volumes down about 25% since March; Q1 FY27 expected to be linear and challenging.
Rupee credit cards eroding forex card share in leisure; RBI parity representation is pending with no timeline.
Margin pressure from new AD-II entrants and FFMC-licensed competitors; trade remittance margins guided at 20-30 bps.
Execution risk on FXC network rollout and trade/family maintenance scope, which management said still has open clarifications.
Management was evasive on FY27 numerical targets, segment-wise volumes, card KPIs and PA-CB licence decision.
Customer service complaint raised on a Delhi branch; management promised corrective action.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the regulatory opportunity and long-term structure, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: Q1 FY27 was flagged as challenging and specific FY27 targets and segment KPIs were withheld. Management was defensive when discussing credit card competition and pricing.
key_quotes: Revenue crossed around INR111 crores for the first time. Revenue grew 26% significantly ahead of GTO growth, good business profitable mix.
We are happy to say we are increasing our market share year-on-year while the business has -- overall market has contracted by 20%.
So, from our perspective, we are clearly focused on forex cards, how to bring out the merits of the forex card and it's up to the customer's choice to take a forex card or credit card.

adds.what: FXC (Forex Correspondent) appointments expanding distribution network over next 12-15 months; not owned branches

growth.why: No numerical FY27 revenue or card targets given; Q1 FY27 guided as challenging with leisure market down ~25% since March and next one to two months tough, while Q4 revenue still grew 22% and trade remittance, FXC expansion and digital mix shift are described without quantified orders or capacity.
